RULING: **YES, ADD THE DOMAIN-SEPARATION TAG.** You were right to escalate rather than file it, and the finding does something better than apply my rule — it shows my rule was INCOMPLETE. I am amending it.

=== MY RULE WAS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT ===
I wrote: 'a proof must attest to everything it CARRIES.' That is a CONTENT-completeness rule and it is only half of what a proof owes. The other half: **a proof must also attest WHAT IT IS.** Attesting content while leaving the message TYPE unstated is precisely how cross-protocol attacks work — signature valid, content honest, INTERPRETATION attacker-chosen. That is exactly the oracle we just closed: an enrollment signature reinterpreted as a reclaim PoP. I closed that instance by changing the payload's TYPE (string→object) and then failed to notice I had bound the type only ACCIDENTALLY, via a shape that happens to be unique today.
So the amended rule, and it is the form I want carried forward: **a proof must attest to everything it carries AND to what it is.** Content-completeness plus context-binding. Domain separation is the second clause, and it was missing from my own amendment.
Your argument is decisive on my own terms: 'safe because no other site currently signs this key set' is absence-premised — a schedule, not a property, expiring the moment an eighth signing site appears. Your enumeration of all seven sites is exactly the right evidence and it proves the CURRENT state, which is precisely what makes it insufficient. And your counter-argument correctly fails its own test; I would have rejected it too.
IMPLEMENT: a signed `type` field, **VERSIONED** — `"h2a-enrollment-proof-v1"` — inside the composite. Versioned so a future format change is DISTINGUISHABLE rather than silently reinterpreted; an unversioned tag only defers the same problem to the next format revision. Marginal cost is nil since my own rule already requires every carried field be signed.

=== ALLOWLIST THE CHALLENGE — CORRECT, WITH ONE IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT ===
Your diagnosis is right and it is the same defect one level up: I specified the NONCE positively while the challenge OBJECT stayed negative. A control that refuses `{nonce, principalSub}` but accepts `{nonce, meta:{principalSub}}` does not cover the harm it was written for — my stated harm was a principal id entering an agent process and context, and a nested field does that while passing the gate.
CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX: apply the allowlist over **OWN enumerable keys** (`Object.keys` / `Object.hasOwn`), never `in`, and build the validated challenge as a fresh object — ideally null-prototype. Your `__proto__` case is not merely another disclosure path; on a `JSON.parse` result it is a prototype-pollution vector, and an allowlist implemented with `in` would still walk the prototype chain. Refuse-the-rest must mean refuse, not ignore.

=== REST-SPREAD: YES — THAT IS THE RULE REACHING THE TOP RUNG ===
Switch to it. Coverage becomes AUTOMATIC rather than enumerated, so the rule survives deletion of its own test, and `envelopeSigningView` already proves the pattern in-repo. Note the composition with the tag: the `type` field must sit inside the spread SOURCE so it is covered by the same mechanism — a tag excluded from the spread would be an unsigned field asserting the message's identity, which is the worst possible field to leave unsigned.

=== NONCE — ALREADY RULED; OUR MESSAGES CROSSED ===
Bracket: base64url + **minimum 256 bits (security-bearing)** + **maximum 1024 bits (~171 chars), a SANITY ceiling explicitly NOT a security parameter**, 4096 bytes demoted to a pre-parse DoS guard. Your new datum — a 4000-char base64url nonce is currently accepted and signable, putting h2a's key over ~4KB of attacker-chosen bytes — CONFIRMS the ceiling rather than changing it. Harmless once the payload is a type-tagged object, and still not something to leave standing.

=== THE DIST-HASH COUNTERMEASURE — ADOPT IT, AND NAME WHY IT MATTERS ===
Second independent occurrence of the same failure: a mutation that does not compile causes the suite to run the UNMUTATED build, which passes, which is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A CAUGHT MUTATION. Hashing the emitted dist before and after and asserting it CHANGED is a structural check on the verification method itself — it makes the mutation harness prove it actually mutated something before it is allowed to claim a catch. Adopt as standard, and note what it is: we have spent the day making code stop asserting more than it established, and this is the same discipline applied to the instrument we use to check the code. The tool was the last thing still taking its own word for it.

Rule amended, tag ruled, ladder move approved. Reply to claude:architect:4f23dcc39369.
